question: What is the ozone layer composed of?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tri-Oxygen**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tri-oxygen refers to **ozone**, a molecule made up of three oxygen atoms (O₃).
 
• Ozone forms a layer in the Earth’s stratosphere known as the **ozone layer**,
 
 
• which absorbs most of the sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation, protecting living organisms from potential damage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Di-oxygen (O₂)**:

 
 
• Di-oxygen refers to the common oxygen molecule consisting of **two oxygen atoms** (O₂).
 
• This is the most stable and abundant form of oxygen in Earth's atmosphere, making up about 21% of the air we breathe.
 
• Di-oxygen is essential for respiration in most living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Tetra-oxygen (O₄)**:
 
 
• Tetra-oxygen refers to a hypothetical or extremely rare form of oxygen that consists of **four oxygen atoms**.
 
• It is not stable under normal atmospheric conditions and doesn't naturally exist in the environment.
 
• Some studies have predicted it might exist under extreme conditions
 
 
 
• **Mono-oxygen (O)**:
 
 
• Mono-oxygen refers to **single oxygen atoms** (O), which are highly reactive and unstable on their own.
 
• Free oxygen atoms typically do not exist independently for long, as they tend to combine with other atoms or molecules to form di-oxygen (O₂) or ozone (O₃).
